claim: For binary \(B_2\)-codes \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^5\), where every coordinatewise ordinary sum \(x+y\in\{0,1,2\}^5\) arising from an unordered pair \(\{x,y\}\) with repetition allowed is distinct, the maximum cardinality is \(12\). Exactly \(192\) labeled maximum codes exist. Under the full Hamming-isometry group \((C_2)^5\rtimes S_5\) of order \(3840\), all \(192\) maxima form a single orbit, so every maximum has stabilizer order \(20\). Every maximum is balanced in each coordinate, contains exactly one antipodal pair, and its \(66\) unordered pairs have Hamming-distance distribution \((5,20,30,10,1)\) at distances \(1,2,3,4,5\), respectively.
integrity: The proof is an exhaustive finite enumeration with an explicit symmetry normalization. The packaged verifier rebuilds the search and checks the complete census and all claimed invariants from scratch using only the Python standard library.
scientific_limitations: Finite dimension-five classification only; no claim is made for larger dimensions or constant-weight subclasses. The exact optimum 12 is previously known; the new content is the complete labeled equality census and isometry structure. Residual bibliographic risk remains for obscure finite classifications not represented in the inspected sources.
title: Equality structure of dimension-five binary \(B_2\)-codes
